body_html:
There are multiple articles around the Web about what has been dubbed “The curse of the 300ms delay”. It’s a delay, the touch-based browser adds to a user-click-interaction.

When you’re clicking on an element in a browser, this is what’s happening:

1. The user touches the display, the browser fires off touchstart
2. The user stops touching the display, the browser fires off touchend
3. The browser waits 300ms to see if the user taps again
4. If the user didn’t tap again, the browser fires off click

For most use-cases this is OK – in the example below, a checkbox has been styled like a switch – using only HTML and CSS:

You should test this on a touch-device.

You’ll notice the grey box around the switch and the label while clicking.
Luckily, this can be disabled with:

-webkit-tap-highlight-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0);

The callout/context-menu can be disabled with:

-webkit-touch-callout: none;

But the 300ms delay is still there. And when you’re aware of it — it seems even longer than 300ms!

There are a number of scripts that can remove the delay and fire the events immediately, the most popular being fastClick and swiftClick.

While these are complex scripts that take a long list of scenarios into account, for my use — the checkbox-hack — a much simpler solution can be used:

/**
*	fastcheck.js
*	Fast checkbox/radio-button-check for touch-devices, removing the 300ms delay
*	(c)	Copyright 2015 Mads Stoumann
*/
(function () {
"use strict";
if("onorientationchange" in window && "ontouchstart" in window) {
	document.body.addEventListener("touchstart", function(e) {
	  	var 
	  	oTarget = e.target,
	  	sTarget = oTarget.nodeName.toLowerCase();
		if (sTarget === "label") window.__activeElement = oTarget;
	}, false);
	
	document.body.addEventListener("touchend", function(e) {
	  	var 
	  	oInput,
	  	oTarget, 
	  	oTouch = e.changedTouches[0];
    	oTarget = document.elementFromPoint(oTouch.clientX, oTouch.clientY);
	
		if (oTarget === window.__activeElement) oInput = document.querySelector("#" + oTarget.getAttribute("for"));
		if (oInput) {
			if (oInput["type"] === "checkbox") {
				oInput.checked = !oInput.checked;
			}
			else if (oInput["type"] === "radio") {
				/* If a radio-button should be unselectable, add attribute: data-unselect="true" */
				oInput.getAttribute("data-unselect") ? oInput.checked = !oInput.checked : oInput.checked = true;
			}
			e.stopPropagation();
			e.preventDefault();
		}
	}, false);
}
})();

The final result can be seen here (if you’re using a desktop-browser, it will be identical to the first example!):

The gzipped and closure-compressed version is 345 bytes.

The script “captures” the clicked element on touchstart, and compares that to the element captured on touchend.

If the element is a label-element and it’s associated input is either a radio-button or a checkbox, that element is clicked immediately.
The normal click-event is then cancelled.

Callback Functions

I usually assign events/functions via a “data-fn”-attribute:

<label for="switch_2" data-fn="myTestFunc" data-pr="My custom parameter">

There’s also a “data-tp”, which defaults to “click”.
Multiple functions (and parameters) are split by “+”, multiple parameters within a function are split on “|”.

If you want to run additional functionality when clicking on a label/checkbox/radio, you can use this slightly longer script (537 bytes gzipped and compressed) and the method described above:

/**
*	fastcheck_fn.js
*	Fast checkbox/radio-button-check for touch-devices, removing the 300ms delay
*	Executes functions in data-fn attributes
*	(c)	Copyright 2015 Mads Stoumann
*/
(function (bRunFunc) { 
"use strict";
if("onorientationchange" in window && "ontouchstart" in window) {
	document.body.addEventListener("touchstart", function(e) {
	  	var 
	  	oTarget = e.target,
	  	sTarget = oTarget.nodeName.toLowerCase();
		if (sTarget === "label") window.__activeElement = oTarget;
	}, false);
	
	document.body.addEventListener("touchend", function(e) {
	  	var 
	  	oInput,
	  	oTarget, 
	  	oTouch = e.changedTouches[0];
    	oTarget = document.elementFromPoint(oTouch.clientX, oTouch.clientY);
	
		if (oTarget === window.__activeElement) oInput = document.querySelector("#" + oTarget.getAttribute("for"));
		if (oInput) {
			if (oInput["type"] === "checkbox") {
				oInput.checked = !oInput.checked;
			}
			else if (oInput["type"] === "radio") {
				/* If a radio-button should be unselectable, add attribute: data-unselect="true" */
				oInput.getAttribute("data-unselect") ? oInput.checked = !oInput.checked : oInput.checked = true;
			}
			e.stopPropagation();
			e.preventDefault();
			if (bRunFunc) getFunc(oTarget), getFunc(oInput);
		}
	}, false);
	
	var getFunc = function(oElm) {
		var
		aFunc,
		aFuncPar,
		aParam,
		i,
		oFunc,
		sFunc = (oElm && oElm.getAttribute("data-fn")),
		sFuncPar;
		
		if (sFunc && !oElm.getAttribute("data-tp")) {
            aFunc = sFunc.split("+");
            sFuncPar = oElm.getAttribute("data-pr");
            aFuncPar = sFuncPar ? sFuncPar.split("+") : [];

            for (i = 0; i < aFunc.length; i++) {
                aParam = aFuncPar[i] ? aFuncPar[i].split("|") : [];
                aParam.push(oElm);
                oFunc = getScope(aFunc[i]);
                aParam.unshift(oElm);
                oFunc.apply(oElm, aParam);
            }
        }
	};
	
	var getScope = function (sFunc) {
		var
		aFunc = sFunc.split("."),
		i,
		oFunc = window[aFunc[0]],
		nLen = aFunc.length;
	
		if (nLen) for (i = 1; i < nLen; i++) oFunc = oFunc[aFunc[i]];
		if (typeof oFunc === "function") return oFunc;
	};
}
})(true);

Disclaimer (!): All the code above have only been tested on Codepen.io, not in a production-environment.
Now, go remove those annoying delays!
